missing_info: pyproject.toml (or the [project] dependencies and any [tool.uv] constraint-dependencies / override-dependencies section) showing how redis[hiredis] is requested
The redis version resolved in uv.lock and the uv.lock entries for redis and hiredis
Output of `uv tree --invert hiredis` (or `uv tree --package hiredis`) showing which package requires hiredis==2.0.0 or an older range
The exact command run (uv sync vs uv lock vs uv pip install) and whether a --upgrade or existing lockfile was in play
Text of the screenshot rather than an image only (the image is the only evidence of the 2.0.0 install)
rationale: The report gives no command, lockfile excerpt, or pyproject, only a summary and a screenshot, so there is nothing a maintainer can reproduce. Package metadata shows the current redis (8.1.0) declares hiredis>=3.2.0 for the hiredis extra, so getting hiredis 2.0.0 means some other pin or an older redis in the reporter's project is forcing it; that is a dependency's constraint, which the playbook treats as a question, not a bug. Searches for the redis/hiredis symptom returned no matching uv issues, and hiredis 2.0.0 metadata shows no requirements, so no external defect is evidenced. The reporter's bug label is not supported by the evidence; confidence is low because the reporter's lockfile and pins were not available to check.
